How it works

Follow the everyday work.

01 / GETTING PAID

Follow a sale through.

Follow a sale from the first quote to the final payment.

  1. Start with a customer request
  2. Prepare a quote
  3. Confirm the customer accepts the quote
  4. Create the invoice
  5. Record the payment
  6. Review the related accounting records
02 / BUYING FROM SUPPLIERS

Keep purchases clear.

Know what you ordered, what arrived and what you still owe.

  1. Choose the supplier
  2. Create a purchase order
  3. Record stock when it arrives (goods received)
  4. Record the supplier invoice
  5. Record the payment
  6. Review the related accounting records
03 / BANKING

Match the money.

Connect transactions on your bank statement to what happened in your business.

  1. Import bank transactions
  2. Review suggested matches
  3. Check the details
  4. Confirm the match
  5. Match your bank and business records

Illustrative journeys, with tools depending on your plan. Bizzy can find records, explain amounts and prepare the next step. You check customers, suppliers, quantities, amounts and tax treatment, then review and explicitly confirm actions that create or change financial or stock records. Recording a payment does not transfer money. Banking uses imported or manually recorded transactions; a live bank feed is not promised.

Everyday language. Professional detail.

You run the business.
O-IBS helps with the books.

You don’t need an accounting degree to get started. Create invoices, record expenses and payments, manage suppliers and keep track of stock. O-IBS keeps the related accounting records organised. Your bookkeeper or accountant can still work with the detailed records and reports available in your plan.

What does this mean? Open an explanation below. Formal names help you recognise the same information in the application.

Money customers still owe youAccounts Receivable

Unpaid amounts on customer accounts. Also labelled Receivables on the dashboard.

Money you still owe suppliersAccounts Payable

Unpaid amounts on supplier accounts.

Money your business earnedRevenue

Income earned from sales, which can differ from money already received.

Day-to-day business costsExpenses

Costs of running your business, such as rent and supplies.

What the products you sold cost youCost of Sales / Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)

The recorded cost of products sold, rather than their selling price.

What your business ownsAssets

Items of value owned by the business, such as equipment, stock and money owed by customers.

What your business owesLiabilities

Amounts the business owes, such as unpaid supplier bills and loans.

What is left after costsProfit

Income earned less the costs for a period. Profit is not necessarily the money available in your bank account.

Match bank transactions to your recordsBank Reconciliation

Check transactions on your bank statement against the records in O-IBS and review differences.

Detailed accounting historyGeneral Ledger

The accounting record of transactions, grouped by account.

Check that accounting entries balanceTrial Balance

Checks whether the debit and credit sides of your records balance. Balanced records can still contain mistakes.

Understand VAT owed or claimableVAT position

The balance of VAT on sales and eligible purchases. It may show VAT owed to SARS or VAT claimable, depending on the records and applicable rules.

See what your business owns and owesBalance Sheet

A snapshot of what the business owns, owes and has built up at a specific date.

See whether the business made a profitProfit & Loss

Shows income earned, costs and the resulting profit or loss over a period.

Review the VAT behind your transactionsVAT Report

Shows recorded VAT on sales and purchases. Check eligibility and tax treatment before relying on it for a return.

Record an accounting adjustmentJournal entry

An adjustment to accounting records. Review the accounts, amounts and reasons before confirming it.

Organise your accounting categoriesChart of accounts

The list of accounts used to group transactions in the detailed accounting records.
